title: Optimized doctor-patient communication - the key to greater willingness to get the RSV vaccine?
summary: Effective vaccines against respiratory syncytial virus have recently been licensed. This study investigates the influence of an optimized education method on vaccination intention and side effect expectancy. Subjects will be randomly assigned to a condition in which either a standard clarification or an optimized clarification will be presented via video. The test subjects are then asked about the expected side effects and vaccination intention.
conditions: Vaccination against the respiratory syncytial virus

interventions.name: Standard clarification (treatment as usual): Presentation as a video recording of a medical clarification consultation in a rational and sober style. Duration of the video approx. 3:15 minutes. N=50 healthy subjects planned.

Optimized clarification: Presentation as a video recording of a clarification consultation with optimized communication (elements: reframing of symptoms, use of primacy/recency effect, strengthening of self-efficacy, empathic interaction). Duration of the video approx. 4:30 minutes. N=50 healthy par

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Sufficient knowledge of German
Exclusion criteria:
Lack of ability to provide consent, severe allergic reactions in the past, presence of an acute infection, patients with a blood clotting disorder, lack of informed consent, inability to participate in the study in the opinion of the study physicians (e.g. acute depression, psychosis)
